assessment:
Four tutors. Drift of Phantasms puts the card in your hand and costs you a 0/5 flying blocker. Enlightened Tutor and Mystical Tutor put it on top. Long-Term Plans buries it third. Three of the four deliver on a schedule, and the schedule is your draw count: the gift assembles in 0.921 of goldfish games, mean turn 2.499, so count the draws per turn before you name a card. Under Font of Mythos a third-from-top card is your next draw step; under Howling Mine, your second; on a bare board, your third.

The win is Approach of the Second Sun cast twice, the second from hand. Enumerated from cards.json: Enlightened Tutor searches for an artifact or enchantment card and Approach is a sorcery; Drift transmutes for mana value 3 and Approach is 7. Mystical Tutor and Long-Term Plans are the two that reach it. Stack 002 (checker pass) settles the second cast: the win is checked as the spell resolves and the stack is the only window. On the 120-game Forge run (v1.2.1, one list behind this one) a first Approach was cast in 27 games, a second in 12, and all 12 were the deck's Approach wins; the other 8 of its 20 wins came from outliving the table. The goldfish's 'Win condition access' reads 0.495 assembled, 0.358 by turn six, and mean available mana crosses 7 between turn 7 (6.412) and turn 8 (7.064) with Heliod's discount switched off. The bind is between the first cast and the second, and every wish below is priced against it.

The other job is living that long. All 61 Forge eliminations were damage, 43 from giada-angels, and the tax layer is the least reliable of the four defensive groups: 0.496 assembled, 0.357 by turn six, against 0.839 (interaction held), 0.683 (Heliod protected) and 0.68 (a flier blocker). Long-Term Plans has no cast line in 160 Forge games and log 002 records the pilot sitting on it. Cast the tutor a turn before it feels necessary, at an opponent's end step.

targets.scenario: The first Approach of the Second Sun resolved earlier this game and sits seventh from the top. It is the end step of the opponent to your right, you have {U} open, and next turn you can pay {6}{W} with a counter still up.
targets.why: This is the card's job. Mystical Tutor searches for an instant or sorcery card and Approach is a sorcery (cards.json). It goes on top; you draw it in your draw step and cast it from hand. Stack 002 (checker pass) is what happens next: the win is checked as the spell resolves, the first cast still counts because the condition reads game history, and the only window anyone gets is while the second Approach is on the stack. Read the split honestly: stack 002 proves the cast, and the search is oracle text - engine.json lines[8] says so. Forge on v1.2.1: 12 games reached a second cast and all 12 won; Mystical Tutor was cast in 38 of 120. Bring the Swan Song or the Dovin's Veto for the counter war and cast nothing else that turn.

targets.scenario: Turn 5 to 7. Two seats have boards, the angels seat has connected once, and your battlefield is artifacts and enchantments with at most one creature on it. You are at 25 or less with {U} spare at an end step.
targets.why: Sweep, because the trade is one-sided. Your board is not your plan, and Verdict cannot be countered, so it resolves into the blue seat's open mana. Forge (v1.2.1): all 61 of this seat's eliminations were damage, combat damage taken mean 37.92 a game, Supreme Verdict cast in 33 of 120 games. Log 002 is the sequencing rule: 'Wipe first, then resolve Heliod' - the pilot killed his own commander with this card. Fetch it at an end step and cast it on your own turn; the tutor buys certainty, not speed. Day of Judgment is the same fetch when the blue seat is tapped out and you want to keep Verdict for later.

targets.scenario: Approach is in your hand off a natural draw, the first cast resolved, and you can reach nine mana next turn: {6}{W} plus {W}{U}. One opponent has held two blue mana open through the whole cycle.
targets.why: Buy the last word, not another threat. Veto cannot be countered and counters a noncreature spell, which is what a counterspell is. Fetch it the end step before you commit, while the table reads a Mystical Tutor as digging. Hold the protection spell for the turn you commit, not after. Held interaction assembles at 0.839, but interaction castable at turn six is 0.61 against 0.929 in hand: the mana is the bind, not the card. Nine mana is a turn-ten figure with the discount off (8.386 mean at turn ten); under the flipped Heliod every opponent draw that turn takes {1} off each spell's generic cost, and a discount never pays a pip. Swan Song does the same job for {U} and hands them a 2/2 Bird - stack 002 step 4 is that line.

citations.quote: hold the protection spell for the turn you commit, not after

targets.scenario: Turn 7 or 8, seven mana available, Approach not in hand and nothing else worth the mana. No opponent is presenting lethal.
targets.why: Fetch the FIRST cast, not the second. The bind is the gap between the two casts, and the first has to happen before the second's clock starts: Forge (v1.2.1) saw a first cast in 27 of 120 games and a second in 12. Mean available mana crosses 7 between turn 7 (6.412) and turn 8 (7.064), so the first turn you can pay {6}{W} is the turn to cast it, and the tutor is not wasted: the first cast gains 7 life and puts the card seventh from the top, where your own gift draws it back - the third draw step under Font of Mythos, the fourth under Howling Mine, sooner again under Alhammarret's Archive or Teferi's Ageless Insight, which double every draw after the first. Long-Term Plans can find it a second time. Log 002 is the failure this wish prevents: 'I waited, got desperate, and the window closed'.

tutors.notes: Instant or sorcery only, and it goes on top: never an answer to what is on the stack now, always an answer for next turn. Teferi's Protection is findable and arrives a turn late; Drift of Phantasms is the tutor that puts it in your hand. NEW at v1.3.0: Mystical Tutor is one of the thirteen instants at mana value 2 or less that Isochron Scepter can imprint (engine.json enumerates them). A Scepter copy at each opponent's end step would put Approach on top for {2} every turn without spending the card. engine.json files that as lines[12] with verified_by null and carries the rules question in open_questions[7]. Status: needs a stack scenario. Do not imprint on that promise until a stack passes; a counter is the imprint that is fact.

targets.scenario: Turn 1 or 2, {W} open at the end step of the opponent to your right. Your hand has lands and a rock and nothing that draws you a card the table is not also drawing.
targets.why: The gift is not the shortage - 'Table draw engine online' assembles at 0.921, mean turn 2.499. The asymmetry is: 'Heliod down with an asymmetric card engine' assembles 0.787 and only 0.583 by turn six, mean turn 5.224. Study is the member of that group whose trigger needs neither Heliod nor an opponent draw: whenever an opponent casts a spell, you draw unless they pay {1}. On the v1.2.1 Forge run it produced 410 trigger lines from 31 games cast. Study over Mystic Remora because Remora's cumulative upkeep takes it off the table within a few turns and Study stays. Cast the tutor at an end step, draw Study, cast it on turn 2 or 3 before anyone has sorted their threats. An early Enlightened Tutor reads as ramp; the reveal tells the table nothing it can act on yet.

targets.scenario: Turn 4 or later. Two seats have boards, you are at 30 or below and falling, and you have already been attacked once because you are the seat with no creatures.
targets.why: Tax the attacker, not the creature. 'A taxer down' is the least reliable of the four defensive groups - 0.496 assembled, 0.357 by turn six, mean turn 4.008 - and it holds three cards: Propaganda, Ghostly Prison and Archangel of Tithes. Enlightened Tutor reaches the two enchantments; Archangel is a creature and belongs to Long-Term Plans. Prison charges {2} per attacker whether it flies or not, which is the point against giada-angels, who caused 43 of this seat's 61 Forge eliminations (v1.2.1). Prison over Propaganda when your open mana is white; the text is identical. It does not stop one large flier whose controller pays the {2} - Swords to Plowshares and Path to Exile are for that.

targets.scenario: A gift permanent is down and every opponent is drawing an extra card a turn. You have a blocker or a tax on the battlefield, and you are two mana short of the turn you want.
targets.why: Bill the table for the cards you handed them. Every opponent draw is {2} or a Treasure, and this deck manufactures those draws: Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Kami of the Crescent Moon, Dictate of Kruphix, Temple Bell, Mikokoro, Kwain, The Second Doctor, Horn of Greed and Scrawling Crawler all fire it. On the v1.2.1 Forge run Tithe was the most-triggered card in the deck: 998 trigger lines from 24 games cast (engine.json). The Treasures carry you from 6.412 mean mana at turn seven to {6}{W} plus a counter on the Approach turn. The condition in the scenario is log 002 verbatim: 'Tithe made me the target immediately and I had no creatures out'. Land it behind a blocker or a tax, or defer it.

targets.scenario: Heliod is flipped, the opponents' draw steps are banking cards, and you hold two cheap instants you would rather cast every turn than once.
targets.why: New at v1.3.0, and the one artifact in the 99 that turns a card into a repeatable ability. Its {2} is generic, so under the back face it is a free flash cast once two opponent draws are banked that turn; its '{2}, {T}' is an activated ability and pays full price every time (oracle text). Thirteen instants at mana value 2 or less are imprint targets (engine.json enumerates them). The imprint that is fact is a counter: Swan Song or Dovin's Veto, a counter every turn for {2} - the counter war in log 001 is what it answers. The imprint that is a candidate is Mystical Tutor, which would put Approach on top every turn: engine.json lines[12], verified_by null. Status: needs a stack scenario. No Forge run has seen the Scepter and the goldfish reads none of the three v1.3.0 cards, so nothing about it is measured.

tutors.notes: The reveal is public and the timing is the information. Cast it on turn 1 or 2 and the table files it as ramp. It costs your next draw step: cast in your own main phase it does nothing until your next turn. It cannot find Approach, and it cannot find a nonartifact creature - not Archangel of Tithes, not Consecrated Sphinx. It can find Lightning Greaves, the one insurance piece the Forge AI used (29 games cast, 41 equips on v1.2.1): equip {0}, shroud, and shroud is yours too - it stops your own Karametra's Blessing and Guardian of Faith on that creature (engine.json open_questions[1], unsettled). It can find either Crawler, both artifact creatures. As a Scepter imprint it is flagged in open_questions[7] as possibly worth nothing; not recommended here.

targets.scenario: The first Approach resolved. Mystical Tutor is in your graveyard or never showed. At least one gift permanent is on the battlefield and you have {2}{U} at an opponent's end step.
targets.why: Third from the top is a schedule. Under Font of Mythos (two additional cards each draw step) Approach is your very next draw; under Howling Mine, Kami of the Crescent Moon or Dictate of Kruphix, your second; on a bare board, your third. Alhammarret's Archive and Teferi's Ageless Insight double every draw after the first in your draw step and collapse it further. Plans is an instant with no reveal - fetch at an end step and keep your own turn for the win. The cost is smaller than it reads: the flipped Heliod takes {1} off generic cost per opponent draw that turn and a discount never pays a pip, so Plans can be {U} and Approach {W}. Log 002, the pilot: 'I should have tutored Approach of the Second Sun to third-from-top immediately. I was overthinking the mana cost'. Long-Term Plans has no cast line in either Forge run - 0 in 160 games - so nothing measured says how often this fires; the goldfish's 'Win condition access' (0.495) counts it drawn, not cast.

targets.scenario: The air is the problem. One or two fliers connect every turn, you have no blocker that reaches them, and a tax alone has not been enough.
targets.why: The one card on both lists. Enumerated from goldfish_targets.json: the flier blockers are Kefnet the Mindful, Drift of Phantasms, Consecrated Sphinx, Faerie Mastermind and Archangel of Tithes; the taxers are Propaganda, Ghostly Prison and Archangel of Tithes. She is the only member of both - a 3/5 flier that charges {1} per attacker while untapped. Mana value 4, a creature, not an artifact: Enlightened Tutor cannot find her, Mystical Tutor cannot, Drift transmutes for 3. Long-Term Plans is the only tutor in the 99 that reaches her. Both groups sit low: flier blockers 0.68 assembled, 0.529 by turn six; taxers 0.496, 0.357. Forge (v1.2.1) cast her in 28 of 120 games. {1}{W}{W}{W} against 21 white land sources (deck-facts): check your white before you bury her.

targets.scenario: Turn 8 or later. The board has stalled behind a tax, you have seven or more mana, and no one can attack anyone for a profit.
targets.why: Close the long game with the table's own draws. Sphinx draws you two on every opponent draw, and the gift guarantees opponent draws. On the v1.2.1 Forge run she produced 326 trigger lines from 25 games cast; Font of Mythos beside her is twelve extra cards a turn cycle for you (engine.json lines[2], a claim with no stack). {4}{U}{U}: goldfish mean mana is 7.064 at turn eight and 8.386 at ten, so this is a turn-eight fetch, not a turn-six one. She is a 4/6 flier and blocks. Only Long-Term Plans reaches her - a creature, not an artifact, mana value 6. Expect the removal: cast her with a counter up or after the wraths are spent.

targets.scenario: Two seats are ahead on board, you are the cheapest attack, and you have no tax or blocker. Four mana available next turn and a gift permanent already down.
targets.why: Buy peace with the gift itself. 'At the beginning of your end step, each player may draw a card. Each opponent who does can't attack you or permanents you control during their next turn.' Every opponent who takes the card cannot attack you next turn; every one who refuses gets no card. He also reads 'Players have no maximum hand size', which Kefnet and Psychosis Crawler both want. Mana value 4, a creature, not an artifact: Long-Term Plans is the only tutor that reaches him. Forge (v1.2.1): 84 heliod-controlled trigger lines (engine.json). He does not stop a seat that would rather attack than draw; the tax layer is for that seat.

tutors.notes: Any card, third from the top, no reveal. It is the only one of the four that finds a creature Drift cannot - enumerated from cards.json, the creatures neither an artifact nor mana value 3 are Archangel of Tithes, Cathar Commando, Consecrated Sphinx, Faerie Mastermind, Kami of the Crescent Moon, Kwain and The Second Doctor - and the only tutor besides Mystical Tutor that finds Approach. Those two jobs compete; decide which one the game is about before you cast it. Zero cast lines in 160 Forge games and one logged game where it stayed in hand: the failure mode of this card is not casting it.

targets.scenario: Your own main phase, {1}{U}{U} spare, Heliod on the battlefield, and two seats are visibly building toward something that ends with your name in it - an alpha strike, a wrath, or a counter war you cannot win.
targets.why: The wish only Drift delivers on time. Transmute puts the card in your hand, so Protection is castable the moment you hold {2}{W}. Mystical Tutor hands it to you a turn late, Long-Term Plans three draws late, Enlightened Tutor cannot find it. The other half of the same rule is the catch: transmute is sorcery-speed, so this happens on your turn, before the thing happens. Fetch it the turn you first suspect. 'Heliod protected, or a flash grant that does not need him' assembles 0.683, 0.531 by turn six; on the v1.2.1 Forge run Heliod's front face resolved in 68 of 120 games and the back face appeared in 35, and Teferi's Protection had no cast line in 120 games - the AI does not hold protection, so Forge's read on this card is a floor. Log 001 is the game it was for: 'I lost the game losing Heliod, in a stack war'.

citations.quote: Discard this card: Search your library for a card with the same mana value as the discarded card, reveal that card, and put it into your hand. Then shuffle your library. Activate only as a sorcery.

targets.scenario: Turn 6 or 7, six mana available, and the pod has gone wide on the ground and in the air. You are the seat with the fewest blockers and everyone knows it.
targets.why: Buy the tax and cast it the same turn: {1}{U}{U} to transmute, {2}{U} to cast, six mana in one main phase. Goldfish mean available mana is 5.764 at turn six and 6.412 at turn seven, so this is a turn-seven play unless a rock is down. The draw-step gifts count nothing on your own turn (engine.json lines[0]); only Temple Bell, Mikokoro, Kwain, Loran or The Second Doctor can feed the discount before your main phase. Propaganda when your open mana is blue, Ghostly Prison when it is white - both are mana value 3 and both are Drift's to find. You are trading a 0/5 flying blocker for it; make the trade when the tax stops more attackers than the body blocks, which against giada-angels (43 of 61 eliminations, v1.2.1) is most turns.

targets.scenario: Heliod is on the battlefield, Approach is in hand for its second cast, and you have no counter for the turn you commit.
targets.why: A free counter for the commit turn. 'If you control a commander, you may cast this spell without paying its mana cost', so the second Approach goes on the stack with every mana spent and a counter still up. It counters a noncreature spell, which a counterspell is; it needs Heliod on the battlefield, which is also what his flash grant needs (Leyline of Anticipation is the other route). Stack 002's window is the only one: a countered Approach yields nothing, and your counter has to win the war. Transmute at sorcery speed the turn before, body given up; Forge (v1.2.1) cast Guardianship in 18 of 120 games. Force of Negation is also mana value 3 and free only when it is not your turn - the wrong turn for a sorcery cast on yours.

targets.scenario: Two gift permanents are down, every hand at the table is full, and the game is going long without a win in sight. Your main phase, {1}{U}{U} spare.
targets.why: The drain is mana value 3. Scrawling Crawler carried the whole life-loss axis on the v1.2.1 Forge run: 851 of 865 drain resolutions - mean 7.44 life a game, median 0.0, nonzero in 47 games, max 104 (engine.json). Off in most games, decisive in a few, and Drift is the tutor that turns a wall into it. It is both halves of the gift-plus-drain component in one card - upkeep draw for everyone, 1 life per opponent draw - and that component is the deck's lowest declared figure: 0.32 assembled, 0.189 by turn six. Enlightened Tutor also finds it (artifact creature), on top rather than in hand. Every card you hand the table now costs them a life; The Second Doctor's offer and Kwain's 'may' become a choice they pay for.

tutors.notes: First decide whether to transmute at all. Drift is a 0/5 flying defender, one of five flier blockers (0.68, 0.529 by turn six), and 43 of this seat's 61 Forge eliminations came from giada-angels. Forge cast it as a body in 35 of 120 games and discarded it 6 times; the record does not say which of those were transmutes. Log 002: 'I played the channel-tutor spirit as a blocker instead of using it to tutor'. The full mana-value-3 list, from cards.json: Archmage's Charm, Decanter of Endless Water, Dictate of Kruphix, Fierce Guardianship, Force of Negation, Ghostly Prison, Guardian of Faith, Horn of Greed, Kefnet the Mindful, Long-Term Plans, Loran of the Third Path, Propaganda, Rhystic Study, Scrawling Crawler, Stroke of Genius, Teferi's Protection, Temple Bell - seventeen. Kefnet is the body that lives through your own Supreme Verdict, if you hold seven cards. Transmuting for Long-Term Plans reaches any card for nine mana across two spells; it is almost never right, and it is how Drift finds Approach. The reveal is public.

gaps: Every Forge figure here is from run b0f44e4a (120 games, pod 'standard', seat decklist_sha256 214af308... = v1.2.1) or 4b0e1964 (40 games, standard-v3, same sha): three cards behind the sleeved list. No Forge run exists on v1.3.0 (f1d4a650...). The goldfish figures are current: goldfish_metrics.json carries decklist_sha256 f1d4a650..., matching deck_versions.paper.

Isochron Scepter imprinting Mystical Tutor is engine.json lines[12] (verified_by null), open_questions[7], and strategic_frame.json candidate_missing_lines[2]. Status: needs a stack scenario. This guide names it twice and asserts it nowhere.

Stack 002 proves the second cast and the counter war; engine.json lines[8] notes Mystical Tutor appears only in the scenario's premise, not in the resolution steps. The search is oracle-text fact and the wish rests on that plus stack 002 for what follows. The stack's board also names Ancient Tomb, which this list does not run; the ruling does not depend on it.

The goldfish's 'Win condition access' (0.495 assembled, 0.358 by turn six) counts any of three cards DRAWN; the deck's win is a second cast with seven mana on two turns. engine.json proposed_goldfish_edits[1] and open_questions[3] carry the request to split it. Quoted here as measured and labelled where used.

The goldfish target label 'A body that can block a FLIER (39 of 53 ...)' carries the v1.0.0 run's figure; the v1.2.1 run reads 43 of 61 (engine.json proposed_goldfish_edits[3]). This guide uses 43 of 61 throughout.

Heliod's discount is not modelled (model-coverage gives him the bodies channel only), so every goldfish mana figure here is a floor; the claim that a cheap generic-cost spell is free on an opponent's turn is oracle-derived and unmeasured.

engine_casts cannot separate a transmute from a discard: Drift of Phantasms shows 6 discards on the v1.2.1 run and no activation line. Long-Term Plans has no line of any kind in either run (engine.json notes[6] calls it the clean case).

Forge floor on protection: Teferi's Protection 0 casts, Guardian of Faith 0 casts, Psychosis Crawler 0 casts in 120 games. Any Forge figure on commander survival or the drain layer's second card is a floor.

strategic_frame.json quotes the gift at 0.898 / 0.79 / 2.639, from before the 2026-09-16 declaration repair; goldfish_metrics.json on disk reads 0.921 / 0.822 / 2.499 and this guide uses the file on disk (engine.json notes[5] records the same gap).
